seo_title: Heartware Network Case Study: Volunteer Brand Voice | SOMIN
description: Fyreflyz used SOMIN to read 1,230 posts for Heartware Network: 87.9% of its posts used the category's two voices, and it had never run a paid placement.
eyebrow: Agency case study · Youth volunteering · Singapore
h1: Heartware puts 87.9% of its posts in two voices, and nobody owns a third
lede: Fyreflyz used SOMIN to read 1,230 posts from Heartware Network, six competitors and seven youth-sector organisations, 1 May to 19 Aug 2026. It found 87.9% of Heartware's posts in the category's two voices, no paid placements in 12 months, and a client hypothesis the data did not support. The pitch delivers three pillars, 12 propositions, a 39-slot Q4 calendar and an SGD 120,000 media plan.
meta_line: A SOMIN agency pitch · 1 May to 19 Aug 2026 · Singapore · Youth aged 14 to 35

stats.label: Heartware posts in the Sage or Caregiver voice

challenge.title: Heartware holds 20.2% of category voice but sounds like the rest
challenge.body: Heartware Network already holds 20.2% of category voice on 132 posts, second only to the Cyber Security Agency of Singapore. But 116 of those posts speak as The Sage or The Caregiver, like most of the category, and Heartware has never run a paid placement. Its own brief assumed skill-based volunteering was open ground.

approach.title: 1,230 posts in three cohorts and a client hypothesis tested
points: Read all 132 of Heartware's organic posts as a census, against 522 posts from six competitors and 576 from seven youth-sector organisations.
Classified every post by archetype, tone, content type and audience, and measured captions for length, calls to action and first-person voice.
Scored nine territories against a whitespace rubric across the three cohorts.
Tested the client's skill-based volunteering hypothesis and checked SOMIN's ads-library index for 12 months of paid activity.
Drew on 20 SOMIN studies across two workspaces to build three insight stories, 12 propositions and 54 creatives.

findings_title: Two voices, a failed hypothesis and a Facebook gap for Heartware

findings.title: 85.2% of competitor and youth-sector posts use two voices
findings.body: 85.2% of the 1,098 competitor and youth-sector posts carry The Sage or The Caregiver. Heartware is at 87.9%, with only 4.5% in Creator, Explorer or Jester, the lowest agency share of the three cohorts.

findings.title: Skill-based volunteering is not whitespace
findings.body: Skill-based volunteering is not whitespace: Heartware sits at 25.0% and competitors at 28.2% on skill-building and career content. Only 1 of 9 territories, restoring self-worth and dignity, clears the whitespace test.

findings.title: One recap: 337 likes on Instagram, 0 on Facebook
findings.body: One recap scored 337 likes on Instagram and 0 on Facebook with identical copy. Facebook takes 22% of output at a mean of 3.1 engagements per post, against 155.1 on Instagram.

delivered.title: An SGD 120,000 media plan, a Q4 calendar and 54 creatives
points: Three pillars weighted by verdict: Unfiltered Stories, Level Up Your Impact and Micro-MAD Moments as a ring-fenced test
12 SOMIN propositions built on three insight stories
A Q4 calendar of 39 dated slots from 1 Oct to 31 Dec 2026, three posts a week, with no dedicated Facebook slots
An SGD 120,000 twelve-month working-media plan with an SGD 33,000 Q4 pilot and three-case KPI projections
54 finished creatives across three pillars and three funnel stages, plus a measurement build plan

quote.text: Everyone bought the lectern and the safety net. Nobody bought the workbench.

outcome.title: Heartware's plan: 45% of budget behind volunteer-authored stories
outcome.body: The plan puts 45% of the budget behind volunteer-authored Unfiltered Stories and 40% behind proof of what a named young person can now do. Micro-MAD Moments runs as a capped SGD 12,000 test with a public readout on 31 Dec 2026. The pitch plans against 520 to 2,792 YouthBank sign-ups over 12 months, as projections, not results.

faq.q: What was wrong with the client's original hypothesis?
faq.a: Heartware believed skill-based volunteering was open ground. SOMIN found Heartware at 25.0% and competitors at 28.2% on that territory, so the verdict was blocked. The pillar was kept and re-founded on proof of what volunteers can now do.

faq.q: Why does Facebook get no dedicated budget line?
faq.a: The same creative and caption scored 337 likes on Instagram and 0 on Facebook. Meta is bought as one inventory pool optimised to Instagram, and Facebook takes spill only.

faq.q: How reliable are the sign-up projections?
faq.a: They are modelled in three cases. The pitch plans against the conservative-to-base band of 520 to 2,792 sign-ups and treats the stretch case of 12,061 as a ceiling, since it exceeds Heartware's onboarding capacity.
